title: Symmetry and repeating patterns in art around the world

figure.name: x-sort
figure.question: What kind of pattern is it?

explain.say: Look at a butterfly, a flower or a carpet. They all have patterns. People in every country make patterns. Look at the board. It shows 3 kinds of pattern.

draw.text: Symmetry and repeating patterns in art around the world

draw.name: x-sort
draw.question: What kind of pattern is it?

explain.say: Look at the first group. It shows mirror symmetry. Fold it down the middle, and both halves match. Butterfly wings have mirror symmetry. So does the front of the Taj Mahal in India. Mexican cut paper flags, called papel picado, often do too.

draw.name: x-sort
draw.question: What kind of pattern is it?

explain.say: Now look at the middle group. It shows turning symmetry. Turn the shape part of the way round. It looks the same again. Many rangoli patterns have turning symmetry. A flower with 5 petals looks the same 5 times in one full turn.

draw.name: x-sort
draw.question: What kind of pattern is it?

explain.say: The last group shows repeating patterns. One shape is used again and again. Kente cloth from Ghana has repeating patterns. So do batik cloth from Indonesia and Roman mosaic floors. Look at your clothes. Can you find a repeating pattern?

draw.name: x-sort
draw.question: What kind of pattern is it?

explain.say: Now make your own repeating pattern. Look at the steps on the board. Pick a shape and draw it again and again. Colour in order, like red, blue, red, blue. Then fold paper, cut a shape and open it. You will see mirror symmetry.

steps.label: Pick a shape
steps.note: A leaf, a star or a zigzag

steps.label: Repeat in a row
steps.note: Draw it again and again, evenly spaced

steps.label: Flip or turn it
steps.note: Try every other one upside down

steps.label: Colour in order
steps.note: Red, blue, red, blue keeps the rhythm

faq.a: Mirror symmetry, or reflective symmetry, means one half is a mirror image of the other, so if you fold along a line, the two halves match exactly.
asks: What is a line of symmetry?

faq.a: Rotational symmetry means a shape looks the same after being turned part of the way round its centre. A five-petal flower looks the same five times in one full turn.
asks: What is the order of rotational symmetry?

faq.a: A repeating pattern uses the same shape, colour or design again and again in a regular way, like stripes, tiles or printed cloth.
asks: What is a pattern in art?
How do I make a repeating pattern?

faq.a: Kente is a colourful woven cloth from Ghana, made of narrow strips woven on looms and sewn together. Its bold repeating patterns and colours carry meanings.
Batik is a way of decorating cloth, famous in Indonesia, where hot wax is drawn on fabric so the dye cannot reach those parts, making beautiful repeating patterns.
asks: Why is batik famous in Indonesia?

facts: UNESCO inscribed Indonesian batik on its list of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2009.
A shape with rotational symmetry of order 4 looks the same four times in one full turn.

quiz.say: You fold a butterfly picture in half. Both halves match. What kind of symmetry is this?
quiz.show: 🦋 Fold in half. Both halves match. Which kind?
quiz.why: Halves that match along a fold show mirror symmetry.

wrong.1: Turning symmetry is about turning a shape, not folding it.
wrong.2: A repeating pattern uses one shape again and again.

quiz.say: Look at the 3 choices. Which one has a repeating pattern?
quiz.show: Which one has a repeating pattern?
quiz.why: Kente cloth uses the same woven shapes and colours again and again.

wrong.1: A single dot happens only once. A pattern repeats.
